newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank urges stronger German equity culture.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank urges stronger German equity culture.

text.p: The Bundesbank on Thursday urged the promotion of a stronger German equity culture, bemoaning the fact that Germany is still lagging miserably behind the world's other economic giants in this regard.
In its January monthly report, the central bank said a stronger emphasis on equity financing would help German firms stave off competition from abroad.

"A broader own-capital basis helps companies to take on entrepreneurial risks and is therefore an important prerequisite for an international competitive position and for accessing markets," the Bundesbank said.
"Moreover an increased flow of funds into the equity market tends to increase efficiency of capital allocation."

The Bundesbank noted that, considering the strength of its economy, Germany's equity market was at the bottom end of the scale among OECD countries, with its market capitalisation just 27 percent of nominal domestic gross domestic product.
Market capitalisation in the U.S., Britain and Switzerland exceeded GDP, often significantly, the report noted.

And while the mega-flotation of telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom AG last November pushed Germany's market capitalisation over the 1,000 billion mark ($625.8 billion) level for the first time, this compares with 13.5 trillion in the U.S.

The Bundesbank also said the situation had barely improved in recent years, with very few small companies in particular managing to make their way to the stock market and with Germans still investing just five percent of their savings in equities.
As a result, the Bundesbank noted that plans to tax capital gains, currently under discussion in Germany, "would have to be regarded critically."

The stock market could prove an increasingly important investment option in years to come as Germany's state pension coffers dwindle and continued globalisation should accelerate the development of a German share culture, the report said.

"The strong public interest connected with the Telekom IPO is a positive thing. But in light of the short-lived impulses sparked by previous placements of 'people's shares', the success of the Telekom flotation should not detract from the fact that promoting share investment is a task that requires lasting effort."
